what_its_for: Triheptanoin is used to treat a rare inherited condition called long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD). In this condition, your body cannot properly break down certain fats for energy. This medicine provides a special type of fat that your body can use as an energy source, helping to reduce symptoms like muscle weakness, heart problems, and dangerously low blood sugar.
how_to_take: Triheptanoin is a liquid that you swallow by mouth. Mix your prescribed dose into a small amount of food or a soft drink before taking it. Do not take it on its own. Spread your daily dose evenly throughout the day, usually given in 3 to 4 small portions with meals or snacks. Use the measuring device provided to measure your dose carefully. Do not use a regular kitchen spoon.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight. The usual starting dose is about 1 gram per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into 3 to 4 doses taken with meals. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to a maximum of 4 grams per kilogram per day depending on how you respond and tolerate the medicine. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store triheptanoin at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep it away from direct sunlight and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children. Use the bottle within 9 months of opening it, or by the expiration date printed on the label, whichever comes first.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping meals while taking this medicine, as it works best when taken with food. Avoid missing doses, as consistent use is important for managing your condition. Talk to your doctor before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements, as some may interact with triheptanoin. Avoid making any changes to your diet without first speaking to your doctor or dietitian, especially changes that affect fat intake.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away; signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, confusion, or fainting; unusual muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine; chest pain or irregular heartbeat; or if your symptoms seem to be getting worse. Also call your doctor if you have trouble mixing or taking your doses as directed.
when_it_works: Triheptanoin begins providing your body with an alternative energy source shortly after you start taking it. Some people notice improvements in energy levels and fewer symptoms within the first few weeks. However, because this is a lifelong condition, you will likely need to take this medicine long-term. It is important to continue taking it every day even if you feel well.
special_populations: Children: Triheptanoin is approved for use in patients of all ages, including newborns and infants. Doses are carefully calculated by weight by your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of triheptanoin during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully studied, so your doctor will help you weigh the benefits and risks. Older adults: There is limited information on use in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you carefully. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver issues, as this may affect how your body handles the medicine.
